quests.instruction: Read: “The glass cup was fragile, but the steel mug was sturdy enough to survive the fall.” Which word in the passage is the opposite of “fragile”?
quests.hint: Which word describes the mug that didn’t break?
quests.explanation: Fragile things break easily. Sturdy things don’t. The passage uses both to compare the cup and the mug.
quests.funFact: Steel is mostly iron mixed with a small amount of carbon.

quests.instruction: In “The knife was too dull to cut the tomato,” which word is the opposite of “dull”?
quests.hint: A knife needs a certain edge to slice a tomato cleanly.
quests.explanation: “Dull” has several meanings: not sharp, not bright, or boring. Here it’s about a knife, so the opposite is sharp.
quests.funFact: Chefs often say a sharp knife is safer than a dull one because it needs less force.

quests.instruction: Riya is faster than Sam. Sam is faster than Tia. Which sentence must also be true?
quests.hint: Line the three runners up from first to last.
quests.explanation: If Riya beats Sam and Sam beats Tia, then Tia is behind both. Faster in one direction is slower in the other.
quests.funFact: In big races, only a few hundredths of a second can separate the winner from second place.

quests.instruction: The team celebrated its victory with a loud cheer. The other team walked off quietly after their…
quests.hint: What do we call losing a match?
quests.explanation: Victory means winning. Defeat means losing.
quests.funFact: “Victory” comes from the Latin word “victoria”.

quests.instruction: During the storm, the little children were ___, but their teacher stayed ___ and kept everyone safe.
quests.hint: Think about who would be helped by a steady voice.
quests.explanation: Frightened children show panic. A teacher who keeps everyone safe stays calm.
quests.funFact: Practicing emergency drills helps people stay calm in real emergencies.

quests.instruction: Which word is NOT an opposite of “happy”?
quests.hint: Two words sit opposite “happy”. One is just a stronger version.
quests.explanation: Sad and gloomy both sit on the opposite side of happy. Delighted is just a stronger way of being happy.
quests.funFact: “Thrilled” and “delighted” are stronger versions of “happy”.

quests.instruction: Warm air makes a balloon expand. If you put the balloon in the freezer, the air inside will…
quests.hint: What happens to the size of air when it gets very cold?
quests.explanation: To expand is to get bigger. To contract is to get smaller. Heat makes most things expand; cold makes them contract.
quests.funFact: Bridges have small gaps called expansion joints so they can change size safely with the temperature.

quests.instruction: Many birds fly south when the weather turns cold. When spring returns, they fly back…
quests.hint: In which direction is the cold place they left?
quests.explanation: North and south are opposite directions. Birds that travel south for winter head north again in spring.
quests.funFact: Arctic terns fly tens of thousands of kilometres between the Arctic and Antarctica every year.

quests.instruction: A pilot flies over the mountains. The miners, working far below them, are ___ the mountains.
quests.hint: Picture where miners work in relation to the surface.
quests.explanation: Over means above something, and under means below it. Miners work beneath the surface.
quests.funFact: Some mines go deeper than three kilometres.

quests.instruction: Exercise helps strengthen your muscles. Staying in bed for weeks without moving can ___ them.
quests.hint: What happens to a muscle you don’t use?
quests.explanation: To strengthen is to make stronger. To weaken is to make weaker.
quests.funFact: Muscles grow stronger when they’re used and given time to rest.

quests.instruction: Complete the saying: “Better late than…”
quests.hint: Think of a word that means zero times.
quests.explanation: The saying says that doing something late is better than not doing it at all, so it pairs “late” with “never”.
quests.funFact: Proverbs often use opposites to make their message easy to remember.

quests.instruction: In the picture puzzle, the red ball was easy to spot. The green ball that blended into the leaves was…
quests.hint: Picture a ball that blends into the leaves.
quests.explanation: Obvious things are easy to notice. Hidden things blend in or are tucked out of sight.
quests.funFact: Camouflage lets animals stay hidden by matching their surroundings.

quests.instruction: A skipping rope must bend easily as you swing it, so it needs to be flexible. Which of these is the opposite, very hard to bend?
quests.hint: Think of the one you couldn’t wrap around your hand.
quests.explanation: Flexible things bend easily. A metal rod is stiff, so it can’t bend into a loop, while the nylon cord and cotton string both bend.
quests.funFact: Many boxers and athletes train with skipping ropes.

quests.instruction: A waterproof jacket keeps rain out. Which of these does the opposite, letting rain pass straight through?
quests.hint: Think of something full of holes.
quests.explanation: Waterproof things stop water getting through. A net is full of gaps, so water passes straight through; the poncho and the boot are both waterproof.
quests.funFact: Rain jackets often use special coatings or tightly woven cloth to keep water out.

quests.instruction: Which sentence means the opposite of “The rocket launch succeeded”?
options: The rocket launch was on TV.
quests.hint: Look for the sentence that says the mission didn’t work.
quests.explanation: To succeed is to achieve what you aimed for. To fail is to fall short. “Delayed” only means later.
quests.funFact: Many rockets are tested several times before carrying people.

quests.instruction: Which sentence means the opposite of “Kiran joined the chess club in June”?
quests.correctAnswer: Kiran quit the chess club in June.
options: Kiran visited the chess club in June.
Kiran won the chess club in June.
Kiran quit the chess club in June.
quests.hint: Which sentence has him leaving instead of becoming a member?
quests.explanation: Joining makes you part of a group. Quitting means leaving it.
quests.funFact: Many clubs let newcomers try a session before deciding to join.

quests.instruction: Which sentence is the opposite of “Ants were everywhere on the picnic blanket”?
quests.correctAnswer: Ants were nowhere to be found on the picnic blanket.
options: Ants were somewhere near the picnic blanket.
Ants were nowhere to be found on the picnic blanket.
Ants were crawling on the picnic basket.
quests.hint: Look for the sentence with zero ants.
quests.explanation: Everywhere means in every place. Nowhere means in no place. “Somewhere” still means they’re there.
quests.funFact: Ants find food by following scent trails laid by other ants.

quests.instruction: In the tug-of-war, Team A kept pulling the rope toward their side, advancing a step at a time. Team B was forced to…
quests.hint: Which way was Team B moving?
quests.explanation: To advance is to move forward. To retreat is to move back.
quests.funFact: Tug-of-war was once an Olympic sport, from 1900 to 1920.

quests.instruction: Complete the instruction: “Use the plus button to enlarge the map and the minus button to ___ it.”
quests.hint: Which button makes the map smaller?
quests.explanation: To enlarge is to make bigger. To reduce is to make smaller.
quests.funFact: Photocopiers can enlarge or reduce a page by a set percentage.

quests.instruction: Which choice describes the opposite of “an ancient temple”?
quests.hint: Which building is the most recent?
quests.explanation: Ancient means from a very long time ago. Modern means from the present day.
quests.funFact: Parts of the Great Wall of China are more than two thousand years old.

quests.instruction: Which choice describes the opposite of “a real diamond”?
quests.correctAnswer: A fake diamond made of glass
options: A fake diamond made of glass
A diamond sold in a shop
A small diamond in a ring
quests.hint: Which one only looks like a diamond?
quests.explanation: A real diamond is genuine. A fake one only imitates it.
quests.funFact: Real diamonds are made of carbon.

quests.instruction: In the school band, the flute plays high notes. The tuba plays…
quests.hint: Which instrument is the bigger of the two?
quests.explanation: High-pitched sounds are thin and squeaky. Deep sounds are low and rumbly.
quests.funFact: Big instruments such as tubas and double basses make lower notes than small ones.

quests.instruction: A park is public: anyone can use it. Which of these is the opposite, meant for one person only?
quests.hint: Think of something with a tiny lock on it.
quests.explanation: Public places belong to everyone. A diary is private: it’s meant for just one person.
quests.funFact: Many diaries come with a small lock to keep them private.

quests.instruction: A complete sentence finishes its thought. A sentence that stops halfway, like “The dog ran across the…”, is…
quests.hint: Does the sentence finish its thought?
quests.explanation: A complete sentence expresses a whole thought. One that stops short is incomplete.
quests.funFact: A full sentence needs a subject and a verb and expresses a complete thought.

quests.instruction: A photograph captures a single moment, so it’s still. A movie is made of pictures that appear to be…
quests.hint: What do the pictures seem to do on the screen?
quests.explanation: Still means not moving. A movie shows pictures so quickly that they seem to move.
quests.funFact: Movies usually show about twenty-four pictures every second.

quests.instruction: Which sentence uses a pair of opposites?
quests.correctAnswer: Grandpa’s hands were wrinkled, but the baby’s skin was smooth.
options: Grandpa’s hands were wrinkled, and so were Grandma’s.
The baby’s skin was soft, and so was her blanket.
Grandpa’s hands were wrinkled, but the baby’s skin was smooth.
quests.hint: Look for the sentence that compares two different things.
quests.explanation: Wrinkled and smooth describe opposite surfaces. The other sentences describe similar things.
quests.funFact: Skin gets wrinkles as it loses some of its stretchiness with age.

quests.instruction: The first half of the match was…, with no goals and few shots. The second half was…, with four goals in ten minutes.
quests.hint: Picture a match with no goals, then a match with lots.
quests.explanation: A match with no action is dull. One full of goals is thrilling.
quests.funFact: Football is the most popular sport in the world.

quests.instruction: The magician will hide the coin in his hand and then ___ it with a flourish.
quests.hint: What does the audience see at the end of a trick?
quests.explanation: To hide is to keep out of sight. To reveal is to show what was hidden.
quests.funFact: Magicians call quick hand moves that hide things “sleight of hand”.

quests.instruction: Which pair has opposite meanings in the sentence “Ravi works quickly, but his sister works carefully and slowly”?
quests.hint: Look for two words that describe different speeds.
quests.explanation: Quickly and slowly describe opposite speeds. The other pairs are just different kinds of words.
quests.funFact: Some artists work for months or years on a single painting.

quests.instruction: Read: “The first question on the quiz was easy, but the last one was very hard.” Which two words are opposites?
quests.hint: Look for two words that describe opposite levels of difficulty.
quests.explanation: Easy and hard describe opposite levels of difficulty. First and last are positions, and the others are unrelated words.
quests.funFact: Teachers often arrange test questions from the easiest to the hardest.
